evidence_items.explanation: Google describes a language-and-vision model directing robotic actions and reports physical robot trials. This satisfies the antecedent under the stated interpretation, without establishing greater risk.

The researchers report attacks eliciting harmful physical actions from LLM-controlled robots. This substantiates a hazard, but supplies no matched estimate of home-assistant risk; the exact experiment dates are not given on the abstract page.

evidence_items.locator: Frontier robot policies reliably carry out harmful instructions
evidence_items.explanation: The evaluation reports refusals and harmful-task completions across five physical-robot tasks. It has no home-assistant control group and explicitly limits generalization beyond its scenes; individual experiment dates are not stated.

The authors report substantial safety improvements in simulated and physical robot experiments. This cautions against treating unguarded robot failures as an inherent comparative disadvantage, but does not compare robots with home assistants; exact experiment dates are unstated.

unresolved_gaps: No located study establishes the risk difference between LLM-controlled robots and comparable conversational home assistants with device-control abilities.
The robot studies measure selected attacks or hazardous instructions, not comparative deployment harm rates.
Marcus supplies no risk measure, representative task distribution or required size of increase.
